mishnayos.summary: There are many ways to say "I will be a nazir." This mishnah lists words that make a person a nazir, even when he does not say the word "nazir" exactly.

chunks.en: All the different ways of saying nezirus count like nezirus.
chunks.st: all substitutes for the language of nazirite vows are like nazirite vows and are binding.
chunks.stMore: Furthermore, intimations of nazirite vows, i.e., incomplete statements that are understood from context to be meant as nazirite vows, are considered binding nazirite vows. Consequently,

words.note: Nezirus: a promise to be a nazir, who may not drink wine, cut his hair, or become tamei from a dead person.

chunks.st: With regard to a woman who vowed to be a nazirite, and

chunks.en: she gets the forty lashes.
chunks.st: she incurs the forty

chunks.en: If her husband canceled her promise,
chunks.st: If her husband nullified her vow,

chunks.he: וְהִיא לֹא יָדְעָה שֶׁהֵפֵר לָהּ בַּעְלָהּ,
chunks.en: and she did not know that her husband canceled it,
chunks.st: and she did not know that her husband had nullified her vow,

chunks.en: and she drank wine and became tamei from dead people,
chunks.st: and she was drinking wine and rendering herself impure by contact with the dead,

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.st: she should incur lashes for rebelliousness [makat mardut],

mishnayos.summary: A woman promised to be a nazir and set aside animals for her korbanos, and then her husband canceled her promise. The mishnah teaches what happens to the animals and to the money she set aside.

chunks.he: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנָּדְרָה בְנָזִיר וְהִפְרִישָׁה אֶת בְּהֶמְתָּהּ
chunks.en: A woman who promised to be a nazir and set aside her animals,

chunks.st: With regard to a woman who vowed to be a nazirite and separated her animals
chunks.stMore: for her offerings of purity at the end of her term,

chunks.en: and after that her husband canceled it:
chunks.st: and afterward her husband nullified her vow,

chunks.en: if the animal belonged to him,
chunks.st: If the animal was his,

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.explain: It is a plain animal again.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock

chunks.en: And if the animal was hers:
chunks.st: And if the animal was hers,
chunks.stMore: different halakhot apply to the various offerings:

chunks.en: the chatas must die,
chunks.st: The animal she set aside as a sin-offering must be left to die
chunks.stMore: by being shut in an enclosed area and deprived of food and water, as will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: the olah is brought as an olah,
chunks.st: And the animal separated for a burnt-offering is sacrificed on the altar as a burnt-offering,

chunks.en: and the shelamim are brought as shelamim,
chunks.st: As for the one designated for a peace-offering, it is sacrificed as a voluntary peace-offering.

words.note: A korban that the owner also eats.

chunks.en: and they are eaten for only one day,
chunks.st: And this peace-offering is eaten for only one day,
chunks.stMore: in accordance with the halakha of the nazirite’s peace-offering, despite the fact that regular peace-offerings may be eaten for two days.

chunks.en: and they do not need loaves of bread.

chunks.en: If she had money set aside but not split up for each korban,
chunks.st: If she had unallocated funds,

chunks.en: the money for the chatas
chunks.st: the money for the sin-offering

chunks.en: is thrown into the Dead Sea.

chunks.en: No one may use it, but using it is not me'ilah.

chunks.stMore: if one did derive benefit from this money he is not liable to bring an offering for misusing consecrated property.

chunks.en: The money for the olah:
chunks.st: As for the money for the burnt-offering,

chunks.en: they bring an olah with it,
chunks.st: a burnt-offering is brought with those coins,

chunks.en: and using it is me'ilah.
chunks.st: and one who benefits from it is liable for misuse
chunks.stMore: of consecrated property, as it is sacred since it can be used toward the purchase of a gift offering.

chunks.en: The money for the shelamim:
chunks.st: Similarly, with regard to the money for a peace-offering,

chunks.en: they bring shelamim with it,
chunks.st: a peace-offering is brought with those coins,

chunks.en: and they are eaten for one day,
chunks.st: and it is eaten for one day and

chunks.en: and they do not need bread.
chunks.st: does not require bread.

mishnayos.summary: A husband can cancel his wife's nezirus. This mishnah teaches until when he can still cancel it, once she has started bringing her korbanos.

chunks.en: Once the blood of one of her korbanos was sprinkled for her,
chunks.st: If the blood from one of her naziriteship offerings was sprinkled on the altar on her behalf,

chunks.en: he cannot cancel anymore.
chunks.st: the husband cannot nullify her vow at this point.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ נִשְׁחֲטָה עָלֶיהָ אַחַת מִכָּל הַבְּהֵמוֹת,
chunks.en: even once one of the animals was shechted for her,
chunks.st: Even before the sprinkling of the blood,

chunks.en: he cannot cancel.
chunks.st: he cannot nullify the vow as soon as any one of the animals for her offerings has been slaughtered on her behalf.

chunks.en: When is this so?
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In what case is this statement, that he can no longer nullify the vow, said?

chunks.en: At the shaving of taharah, at the end of her nezirus.
chunks.st: It is when she is bringing the offerings for her shaving of ritual purity,
chunks.stMore: when she has completed her term of naziriteship without becoming ritually impure (see Numbers 6:18).

chunks.en: But at the shaving of tumah, he can cancel,
chunks.explain: She became tamei and must start her nezirus over.
chunks.st: However, if she is sacrificing the offerings for her shaving of impurity, when she became ritually impure during her term of naziriteship, after which she restarts her naziriteship (see Numbers 6:9), her husband can nullify her vow.

chunks.en: because he can say,
chunks.st: The reason is that he can say:

chunks.en: "I don't want a sad wife."
chunks.explain: She would have to stay away from wine for a long time.
chunks.st: I do not want a downcast [menuvvelet] wife,
chunks.stMore: who does not drink wine. She would have to refrain from wine for a lengthy period if she were to begin her naziriteship anew.

chunks.en: Rebbi says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: even at the shaving of taharah he can cancel,

chunks.en: because he can say,

chunks.en: "I don't want a wife with a shaved head."
chunks.st: I do not want a shaven wife,

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna discussed the case of a husband who nullified his wife’s vow after she separated her offerings of naziriteship. This mishna deals with a husband who nullified his wife’s naziriteship after she had completed her term and brought her offerings to the Temple.

mishnayos.summary: A father can make his young son a nazir, but a mother cannot. If the son refuses, the nezirus ends, and the mishnah teaches what happens to the animals and money set aside.

chunks.en: A man can make his son a nazir,
chunks.st: A man can vow that his minor son should be a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a father can declare his son a nazirite,

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מַדֶּרֶת אֶת בְּנָהּ בְּנָזִיר.
chunks.en: but a woman cannot make her son a nazir.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot vow that her son should be a nazirite.

chunks.en: How is it? If the son shaved, or his relatives shaved him,
chunks.st: How so; what are the details of this naziriteship? If the son shaved his hair, thereby demonstrating his rejection of the vow imposed by his father; or if his relatives shaved him;

chunks.en: or he said no, or his relatives said no,
chunks.explain: Then the nezirus is canceled.
chunks.st: or if the son objected by saying that he has no desire for this naziriteship; or if his relatives objected on his behalf, the naziriteship is canceled.

chunks.en: if he had an animal set aside:
chunks.st: If this son who canceled the naziriteship had animals separated for his offerings,

chunks.en: the chatas must die,
chunks.st: the one set aside for the sin-offering must die,

chunks.en: the olah is brought as an olah,
chunks.st: and the burnt-offering is sacrificed as a burnt-offering,

chunks.en: and the shelamim are brought as shelamim,
chunks.st: and the peace-offering is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

chunks.en: and they are eaten for one day,
chunks.st: And the peace-offering is eaten for one day,
chunks.stMore: like the peace-offering of a nazirite, rather than the two days of a regular peace-offering,

chunks.en: and they do not need bread.
chunks.st: and it does not require bread,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the loaves that accompany a nazirite’s peace-offering.

chunks.en: If he had money not split up for each korban,
chunks.st: If he had unallocated funds,

chunks.en: it goes for gift korbanos.
chunks.st: they will be allocated for communal gift offerings.

chunks.en: If it was split up:
chunks.st: If he had allocated funds for his offerings,

chunks.en: the money for the chatas goes into the Dead Sea;
chunks.st: the money for the sin-offering is taken and cast into the Dead Sea,

chunks.en: no one may use it, but using it is not me'ilah.
chunks.st: as one may not benefit from it ab initio, but if he benefits from it, he is not liable to bring an offering for misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: The money for the olah:
chunks.st: With the money for the

chunks.en: they bring an olah, and using it is me'ilah.
chunks.st: burnt-offering they bring a burnt-offering; it is prohibited to derive benefit from those coins and if he benefits from it, he is liable to bring an offering for misuse of consecrated property.

chunks.en: The money for the shelamim:
chunks.st: With the money for the

chunks.en: they bring shelamim,
chunks.st: peace-offering they bring a peace-offering,

chunks.en: and they are eaten for one day,
chunks.st: and it is eaten for one day and

chunks.en: and they do not need bread.
chunks.st: does not require bread.

mishnayos.summary: A son can use the money his father set aside for nezirus korbanos, but a daughter cannot. Rabbi Yosei explains exactly when this is.

chunks.en: A son can shave using his father's nezirus money,
chunks.explain: He uses money his father set aside for his own nazir korbanos.
chunks.st: A man can shave, i.e., bring the offerings at the close of his term of naziriteship, by using offerings originally designated for his father’s naziriteship,

chunks.he: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מְגַלַּחַת עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיהָ.
chunks.en: but a daughter cannot shave using her father's nezirus.
chunks.st: but a woman cannot shave by means of the offerings for her father’s naziriteship.

chunks.en: How is it? Someone whose father was a nazir,
chunks.st: How so; how is this halakha applied? It applies to one whose father was a nazirite

chunks.he: וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת סְתוּמִים עַל נְזִירוּתוֹ וּמֵת,
chunks.en: and set aside money, not split up, for his nezirus, and died,
chunks.st: and separated unallocated money for his naziriteship, i.e., he did not state which coins were for which of his offerings, and he died before buying the animals,

chunks.en: and the son said, "I am a nazir
chunks.st: and the son said after his father’s death: I am hereby a nazirite

chunks.he: עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲגַלַּח עַל מְעוֹת אַבָּא,
chunks.en: on condition that I shave with Abba's money,"
chunks.st: on the condition that I will shave by means of the money that my father set aside.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: this money goes for gift korbanos;
chunks.st: In that case these coins are allocated for communal gift offerings,

chunks.he: אֵין זֶה מְגַלֵּחַ עַל נְזִירוּת אָבִיו.
chunks.en: this is not "shaving with his father's nezirus."
chunks.st: and the son may not use them, as this is not the case of the halakha that a son can shave by using his father’s naziriteship.

chunks.en: Who is the one who shaves with his father's nezirus?
chunks.st: Rather, who is the son who can shave by using his father’s naziriteship?

chunks.en: Someone who was a nazir together with his father,
chunks.st: This is referring to a son and his father who were both nazirites during his father’s lifetime,

chunks.he: וְהִפְרִישׁ אָבִיו מָעוֹת סְתוּמִים לִנְזִירוּתוֹ וּמֵת,
chunks.en: and his father set aside money, not split up, for his nezirus, and died.
chunks.st: and his father separated unallocated money for his naziriteship and died;

chunks.en: This is the one who shaves with his father's nezirus.
chunks.st: this is the one who may shave by using his father’s naziriteship.

mishnayos.summary: Beis Shammai say that something made hekdesh by mistake is still hekdesh, and Beis Hillel say it is not. For example, a man said the first black ox to come out would be hekdesh, and a white one came out.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: hekdesh made by mistake is still hekdesh.
chunks.st: Consecration that one performs in error nevertheless renders property consecrated,

words.note: Something given to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say

chunks.en: it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: How is it? He said,
chunks.st: How so; what is considered an act of erroneous consecration? If one said:

chunks.en: "The black ox that comes out of my house
chunks.st: A black bull that will emerge from my house

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: first is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a white one came out.
chunks.st: and a white bull emerged first,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

mishnayos.summary: More examples of hekdesh by mistake: he said a gold coin, and a silver one came up; he said a barrel of wine, and a barrel of oil came up.

chunks.en: "The gold dinar that comes up in my hand
chunks.st: Similarly, if one said: A gold dinar that will come up first in my hand

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a silver one came up:
chunks.st: and when he reached into his pocket a dinar of silver came up,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

chunks.en: "The barrel of wine that comes up in my hand
chunks.st: Likewise, if one said: A barrel of wine that will come up first in my hand

chunks.en: first will be hekdesh,"
chunks.st: when I enter the cellar is consecrated,

chunks.en: and a barrel of oil came up:
chunks.st: and a barrel of oil came up in his hand instead,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say it is hekdesh,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated

chunks.en: and Beis Hillel say it is not hekdesh.
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say it is not consecrated.

mishnayos.summary: If a Sage undoes someone's nezirus, the animal he set aside becomes a plain animal again. Beis Hillel use this to argue with Beis Shammai about hekdesh made by mistake, and Beis Shammai answer with the animals of maaser.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁנָּדַר בְּנָזִיר וְנִשְׁאַל לְחָכָם וַאֲסָרוֹ,
chunks.en: Someone who promised to be a nazir asked a Sage, and the Sage said he must keep it:
chunks.explain: He had stopped keeping it, hoping it would be undone.
chunks.st: With regard to one who took a vow of naziriteship, who then regretted his vow and stopped observing the prohibition against drinking wine, and later requested of a halakhic authority to dissolve his vow, and the authority ruled that he is bound by his vow, finding no reason to dissolve it,

chunks.en: he counts from the time he made the promise.
chunks.st: he counts the term of naziriteship from the time that he vowed,
chunks.stMore: including the days when he acted as though the vow were dissolved.

chunks.en: If he asked a Sage and the Sage undid it,
chunks.st: In a case where he requested of a halakhic authority to dissolve his vow and the authority dissolved it,

chunks.en: if he had an animal set aside,
chunks.st: if he had an animal separated as a nazirite offering

chunks.en: it goes out and grazes with the flock.
chunks.st: it shall go out and graze among the flock.
chunks.stMore: On the basis of this halakha, and continuing their discussion in the previous mishna,

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to Beis Shammai,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:

chunks.en: "Don't you agree in this case
chunks.st: Don’t you concede with regard to this case

chunks.en: that it is hekdesh by mistake,
chunks.st: that it is an erroneous act of consecration,

chunks.en: and it goes out and grazes with the flock?"
chunks.st: and yet the halakha is that it shall go out and graze among the flock?
chunks.stMore: This shows that you too accept the principle that an erroneous act of consecration does not take effect.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai said to Beit Hillel:

chunks.en: "Don't you agree about someone who made a mistake
chunks.explain: He was counting his animals to make every tenth one maaser.
chunks.st: Don’t you concede with regard to one who was separating the animal tithe from his herd, i.e., passing his animals before him single file and consecrating every tenth one as a tithe, that if he erred

chunks.en: and called the ninth "tenth," and the tenth "ninth,"
chunks.st: and called the ninth animal: Tenth; and the tenth: Ninth;

chunks.en: and the eleventh "tenth,"
chunks.st: and the eleventh: Tenth,

chunks.en: that it is holy?"
chunks.explain: This shows that hekdesh by mistake counts.
chunks.st: that each of them is consecrated?
chunks.stMore: This proves that an erroneous act of consecration does take effect.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel said to them,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel said to them:

chunks.en: "It is not the stick that makes it holy.
chunks.explain: He counted the animals with a stick.
chunks.st: It is not the rod that consecrates it.
chunks.stMore: The touch of the rod does not consecrate the animal, nor does the fact that he said: Tenth, by mistake. Not all errors cause the tithe to be consecrated, and the proof is as follows:

chunks.he: וּמָה אִלּוּ טָעָה וְהִנִּיחַ אֶת הַשֵּׁבֶט
chunks.en: What if he made a mistake and put the stick
chunks.st: And what would be the halakha if he had erred and placed the rod

chunks.en: on the eighth or the twelfth?
chunks.st: on the eighth or on the twelfth, and labeled them: Tenth?

chunks.en: Did he do anything?
chunks.explain: The eighth or the twelfth does not become maaser.
chunks.st: Can it be suggested that perhaps he performed anything
chunks.stMore: of consequence? The halakha is that the eighth or twelfth animal cannot be consecrated as tithe.

chunks.en: Rather, the same pasuk that made the tenth holy
chunks.st: Rather, why is the ninth or eleventh animal consecrated? There is a specific reason for this halakha, as the same verse that consecrated the tenth

chunks.en: made the ninth holy
chunks.st: also consecrated the ninth

chunks.en: and the eleventh."
chunks.st: and the eleventh.
chunks.stMore: It is a Torah edict that the consecration takes effect with regard to those two animals. Therefore, one cannot infer from this case that an erroneous act of consecration takes effect.

mishnayos.summary: A man promised to be a nazir and then found that the animal for his korban was stolen. The mishnah teaches when this undoes his promise, and tells how Nachum HaMadi made a mistake about nazirs after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed.

chunks.en: Someone who promised to be a nazir
chunks.st: With regard to one who took a vow of naziriteship

chunks.en: and went to bring his animal,
chunks.st: and went to bring his animal which he set aside for his nazirite offering

chunks.en: and found that it was stolen:
chunks.st: and discovered that it was stolen,
chunks.stMore: and due to the need to separate an additional animal now regrets having taken his vow,

chunks.he: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְנְבָה בְהֶמְתּוֹ נָזַר,
chunks.en: if he made the promise before his animal was stolen,
chunks.st: if he took a vow of naziriteship before his animal was stolen,

chunks.en: he is a nazir.
chunks.st: he is a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: as a vow cannot be dissolved as the result of a later event.

chunks.en: But if he made the promise after his animal was stolen,
chunks.st: But if he took a vow of naziriteship after his animal was stolen,

chunks.en: he is not a nazir.
chunks.explain: He promised by mistake, counting on an animal he did not have.
chunks.st: he is not a nazirite,
chunks.stMore: as it is retroactively established that his vow was taken in error from the outset, as he relied on an animal he did not possess.

chunks.en: This was the mistake that Nachum HaMadi made.
chunks.st: And this was the error that Naḥum the Mede erred
chunks.stMore: when he failed to distinguish between an event that occurred before the vow was taken and an event that occurred afterward.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: If he brought three animals and did not say which is for which korban,
chunks.st: If a nazirite brought three animals without specifying which of them was for which offering,

chunks.en: the one that fits a chatas is brought as a chatas,
chunks.st: the one that is fit for a sin-offering, i.e., a female sheep in its first year, is sacrificed as a sin-offering;

chunks.en: the one that fits an olah is brought as an olah,
chunks.st: that which is fit for a burnt-offering, a male sheep in its first year, is sacrificed as a burnt-offering;

chunks.en: and the one that fits shelamim is brought as shelamim.
chunks.st: and that which is fit for a peace-offering, a ram, i.e., a male sheep over the age of one year, is sacrificed as a peace-offering.

chunks.en: He would take the hair of his nazir head
chunks.st: After the nazirite shaved off his hair, he would take the hair of his consecrated head

chunks.en: and throw it under the pot.
chunks.explain: The shelamim was cooking in the pot, so the hair burned in its fire.
chunks.st: and throw it under the pot
chunks.stMore: in which the peace-offering was cooked, where it would burn.

chunks.en: And if he shaved outside the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: And if the nazirite shaved in the rest of the country, i.e., outside the Temple,

chunks.en: he would not throw it under the pot.
chunks.st: he would not throw the hair under the pot.
chunks.basisNote: Our Hebrew text has no "not" here; Steinsaltz and Bartenura both explain that he does not throw it.

chunks.en: When is this so?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: At the shaving of taharah.
chunks.st: It is said with regard to the shaving of purity.

chunks.en: But at the shaving of tumah,
chunks.st: However, with regard to the shaving of impurity,
chunks.stMore: i.e., shaving that accompanied his guilt-offering and sin-offering of birds after his term of naziriteship was interrupted by impurity,

chunks.en: he would not throw it under the pot.
chunks.st: he would not throw his hair under the pot
chunks.stMore: in which his offerings were cooked, as the Torah stated this requirement only for a pure nazirite.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: everyone throws it under the pot,
chunks.st: Everyone throws his hair under the pot,
chunks.stMore: including a pure nazirite who shaved outside the Temple and an impure nazirite,

chunks.en: except only a tamei nazir who shaved outside.
chunks.st: except for an impure nazirite who shaved in the rest of the country. In that case alone
chunks.stMore: he refrains from throwing his hair to be burned beneath his offering.

mishnayos.summary: The Kohen waves the cooked foreleg of the ram and two matzos on the nazir's hands, and then the nazir may drink wine again. Rabbi Shimon says he may already drink once the blood of one korban was sprinkled.

chunks.he: הָיָה מְבַשֵּׁל אֶת הַשְּׁלָמִים אוֹ שׁוֹלְקָן.
chunks.en: He would cook the shelamim, or boil it well.
chunks.st: The nazirite would cook the peace-offering or overcook it, i.e., cook it thoroughly.

chunks.he: הַכֹּהֵן נוֹטֵל אֶת הַזְּרוֹעַ בְּשֵׁלָה מִן הָאַיִל,
chunks.en: The Kohen takes the cooked foreleg of the ram,
chunks.st: The priest takes the cooked foreleg from the ram,

chunks.en: and one matzah loaf from the basket,
chunks.st: and one unleavened loaf from the basket,

chunks.en: and one matzah wafer,
chunks.st: and one unleavened wafer,

chunks.en: and puts them on the nazir's palms and waves them.
chunks.st: and places them on the palms of the nazirite and waves them, as described in the Torah (Numbers 6:19–20).

chunks.en: After that the nazir is allowed
chunks.st: And afterward the nazirite is permitted

chunks.en: to drink wine and to become tamei from dead people.
chunks.st: to drink wine and to contract ritual impurity imparted by a corpse.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:

chunks.he: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים,
chunks.en: as soon as the blood of one korban is sprinkled for him,
chunks.st: Once the blood of one of the offerings has been sprinkled on the nazirite’s behalf,

chunks.he: הֻתַּר הַנָּזִיר לִשְׁתּוֹת בְּיַיִן וּלְהִטַּמֵּא לְמֵתִים:
chunks.en: the nazir may drink wine and become tamei from dead people.
chunks.st: the nazirite is permitted to drink wine and to contract ritual impurity imparted by a corpse.
chunks.stMore: The rest of the ritual is not indispensable for his purification.

mishnayos.summary: If a nazir shaved after a korban that turned out to be pasul, his shaving does not count. Rabbi Shimon says that only that one korban does not count.

chunks.en: If he shaved after the korban, and it turned out to be pasul,
chunks.st: If a nazirite shaved based upon the requisite offering, and afterward the offering was found to be invalid for any reason,

words.note: Not kosher for a korban.

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.en: If he shaved after a chatas that was brought not for its own sake,
chunks.explain: It was brought with the wrong korban in mind.
chunks.st: If he shaved based upon the sin-offering, that was found to have been sacrificed not for its own sake, which invalidates the offering,

chunks.en: and after that he brought his korbanos for their own sake,
chunks.st: and afterward he brought his other offerings for their own sake,

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his other offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.he: גִּלַּח עַל הָעוֹלָה אוֹ עַל הַשְּׁלָמִים
chunks.en: If he shaved after the olah or the shelamim
chunks.st: If he shaved based upon the requisite burnt-offering or having brought the requisite peace-offering,

chunks.en: that were brought not for their own sake,
chunks.st: and these were offered not for their own sake,

chunks.en: and after that he brought his korbanos for their own sake,
chunks.st: and afterward he brought his remaining offerings for their own sake,

chunks.en: his shaving does not count,
chunks.st: his shaving is invalid

chunks.en: and his korbanos do not count for him.
chunks.st: and his offerings do not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says:
chunks.stMore: In the case of one who shaved based upon a burnt-offering or a peace-offering that was sacrificed not for its own sake,

chunks.en: that korban does not count for him,
chunks.st: that offering, which was performed incorrectly, does not count toward the fulfillment of his obligation;

chunks.en: but his other korbanos do count.
chunks.st: however, his other offerings do count.

chunks.en: And if he shaved after all three,
chunks.st: And everyone agrees that if he shaved based upon all three of them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he brought all three offerings, without specifying which offering he is basing his shaving upon,

chunks.en: and even one of them turned out kosher,
chunks.st: and even one of them was found valid,

chunks.en: his shaving counts,
chunks.st: his shaving is valid,

chunks.en: and he must bring the other korbanos.
chunks.st: but he must bring the other offerings in order to fulfill his obligation.

mishnayos.stIntro: As taught earlier (45a) the nazirite shaves after having brought one, or all, of his offerings. This mishna discusses what the halakha is if the offering was found to be invalid after the nazirite had shaved.

mishnayos.summary: If a nazir became tamei after the blood of one of his korbanos was sprinkled, Rabbi Eliezer says he loses all his days. The Sages say he brings the rest of his korbanos, as happened with Miriam of Tarmod.

chunks.he: מִי שֶׁנִּזְרַק עָלָיו אֶחָד מִן הַדָּמִים
chunks.en: Someone for whom the blood of one korban was sprinkled,
chunks.st: With regard to one on whose behalf the blood of one of his nazirite offerings was sprinkled on the altar,

chunks.en: and then he became tamei:
chunks.st: and he became ritually impure before bringing the rest of his offerings,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: it undoes everything.
chunks.st: His impurity negates the entire tally, and he remains a nazirite.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he brings the rest of his korbanos and becomes tahor.
chunks.st: Let him bring the rest of his offerings and be purified.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Eliezer:

chunks.en: There was a story with Miriam of Tarmod,
chunks.st: An incident occurred involving Miriam of Tarmod who was a nazirite,

chunks.en: that the blood of one of her korbanos was sprinkled for her,
chunks.st: that the blood of one of her offerings was sprinkled on her behalf,

chunks.en: and people came and told her
chunks.st: and they came and told her

chunks.en: that her daughter was very sick.
chunks.st: that her daughter was mortally ill.

chunks.en: She went and found that she had died.
chunks.explain: So Miriam became tamei.
chunks.st: And she went and found that her daughter was dead, and thereby contracted impurity.

chunks.en: And the Sages said,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis said:

chunks.en: "She should bring the rest of her korbanos and become tahor."
chunks.st: Let her bring the rest of her offerings and be purified.

mishnayos.summary: A Kohen Gadol and a nazir may not become tamei even for their relatives, but they must bury a mes mitzvah. If both find one together, Rabbi Eliezer and the Sages argue which of them should do it.

chunks.he: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְנָזִיר אֵינָן מִטַּמְּאִין לִקְרוֹבֵיהֶן,
chunks.en: A Kohen Gadol and a nazir may not become tamei for their relatives,
chunks.explain: Even when a close relative passes away.
chunks.st: A High Priest and a nazirite may not become ritually impure even to bury their deceased relatives.

chunks.en: but they do become tamei for a mes mitzvah.
chunks.explain: A mes mitzvah is a dead person with nobody else to bury him.
chunks.st: However, they become impure to bury a corpse with no one to bury it [met mitzva].
chunks.stMore: If one of them comes across the corpse of a Jew, and there is nobody else available to bury it, he must bury the body.

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְהַלְּכִין בַּדֶּרֶךְ וּמָצְאוּ מֵת מִצְוָה,
chunks.en: If they were walking on the road and found a mes mitzvah,
chunks.st: If a High Priest and a nazirite were walking along the way and they found a met mitzva,
chunks.stMore: and one of them can tend to the burial by himself,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.he: יִטַּמָּא כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל וְאַל יִטַּמָּא נָזִיר.
chunks.en: let the Kohen Gadol become tamei, and not the nazir.
chunks.st: Let the High Priest become impure, and do not let the nazirite become impure.

chunks.en: And the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: יִטַּמָּא נָזִיר וְאַל יִטַּמָּא כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל.
chunks.en: let the nazir become tamei, and not the Kohen Gadol.
chunks.st: Let the nazirite become impure, and do not let even a common priest become impure.
chunks.basisNote: Steinsaltz's text reads "not even a regular Kohen."

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said to them,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Rabbis:

chunks.en: "Let the Kohen become tamei,
chunks.st: It is preferable to let the priest become impure,

chunks.en: since he does not bring a korban for his tumah,
chunks.st: as he does not bring an offering for his impurity,

chunks.en: and not the nazir,
chunks.st: and do not let the nazirite become impure,

chunks.en: since he brings a korban for his tumah."
chunks.st: as he brings an offering for his impurity.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to him: On the contrary,

chunks.he: יִטַּמָּא נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין קְדֻשָּׁתוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת עוֹלָם,
chunks.en: "Let the nazir become tamei, since his holiness is not forever,
chunks.explain: His nezirus ends after a while.
chunks.st: let the nazirite become impure, as his sanctity is not permanent,

chunks.he: וְאַל יִטַּמָּא כֹהֵן שֶׁקְּדֻשָּׁתוֹ קְדֻשַּׁת עוֹלָם:
chunks.en: and not the Kohen, since his holiness is forever."
chunks.st: and do not let a priest become impure, as his sanctity is permanent.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the kinds of tumah from a dead person that make a nazir shave, undo his days, and bring korbanos.

chunks.en: For these kinds of tumah a nazir shaves:
chunks.st: A nazirite shaves for having become impure from these following sources of ritual impurity:

chunks.en: for a dead body,
chunks.st: For having become impure with impurity imparted by a corpse;

chunks.en: for a kezayis of a dead body,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by an olive-bulk of a corpse;

chunks.en: for a kezayis of netzel,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by an olive-bulk of fluid [netzel] from a corpse;

words.note: Liquid that comes from a dead body.

chunks.en: for a full spoon of rakav,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by a full ladle [tarvad] of dust from a corpse;

words.note: Dust from a dead body.

chunks.en: for the backbone and for the skull,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by the spine; and for impurity imparted by the skull;

chunks.en: for a limb from a dead person,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by a limb from a corpse

chunks.en: or a limb from a living person,
chunks.st: or for impurity imparted by a limb severed from a living person,

chunks.en: that has the right amount of flesh on it,
chunks.st: upon either of which there is a fitting quantity of flesh;

chunks.en: for half a kav of bones,
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by a half-kav of bones from a corpse;

words.note: A measure, about the size of a few eggs.

chunks.en: and for half a log of blood.
chunks.st: and for impurity imparted by a half-log of blood.

words.note: A measure, the size of a few eggs.

chunks.he: עַל מַגָּעָן וְעַל מַשָּׂאָן וְעַל אָהֳלָן,
chunks.en: He shaves for touching them, carrying them, or being under one roof with them.
chunks.st: And a nazirite shaves in each of these cases for becoming impure by coming into contact with them; and for becoming impure by carrying them; and for becoming impure by their tent,
chunks.stMore: i.e., if he was positioned like a tent over them, or if he entered a tent that contains them, or if they served as a tent over him.

chunks.en: And for a bone the size of a barley grain,
chunks.st: And as for a bone that is a barley-grain-bulk,

chunks.en: he shaves for touching it or carrying it.
chunks.st: he shaves for becoming impure by coming into contact with it and by carrying it.
chunks.stMore: However, he is not rendered impure with the impurity imparted in a tent, i.e., by being under the same roof as the bone.

chunks.en: For these a nazir shaves,
chunks.st: For all of these occurrences, a nazirite shaves, and

chunks.en: and he is sprinkled on the third and seventh days,
chunks.st: a priest sprinkles the ashes of the red heifer on him on the third and on the seventh
chunks.stMore: days to purify him from the impurity imparted by a corpse.

chunks.en: and he undoes the days before,
chunks.st: And he negates all the previous days he counted toward his naziriteship,

chunks.en: and he does not start counting again
chunks.st: and he begins counting his term of naziriteship again

chunks.en: until he becomes tahor
chunks.st: only after he becomes pure

chunks.en: and brings his korbanos.
chunks.st: and brings his offerings.

mishnayos.summary: For some kinds of tumah that are weaker or not certain, a nazir does not shave and does not lose his days. He is sprinkled and goes right on counting.

chunks.en: But for overhanging branches,
chunks.explain: We are not sure if a dead body is under them.
chunks.st: However, the nazirite does not shave for these: The hanging branches over a corpse,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a tree overhanging a body that a nazirite passes, but it is uncertain which branches are over a corpse;

chunks.en: stones sticking out of walls, a beis haperas,
chunks.st: and the projecting stones from fences when the place of the impurity is unknown; and a beit haperas,
chunks.stMore: a place that contained a grave and was plowed. In the latter case, the entire area around the grave is impure from a corpse due to an uncertainty, as it might contain human bones. The mishna continues its list:

words.note: A field where a grave was plowed up.

chunks.en: lands outside Eretz Yisrael,
chunks.st: And the land of the nations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., a nazirite left Eretz Yisrael for another land. The Sages decreed that all land outside of Eretz Yisrael is ritually impure.

chunks.en: the cover of a grave and its side stones,
chunks.st: And the grave cover; and the grave walls upon which the cover rests;

chunks.en: a revi'is of blood,
chunks.st: and a quarter-log of blood from a corpse;

chunks.en: a tent, a quarter-kav of bones,
chunks.st: and a tent; and a quarter-kav of bones of a corpse;

chunks.en: things that touch a dead body,
chunks.st: and vessels that are touching a corpse.

chunks.en: the days of his counting,
chunks.explain: The seven days a metzora counts to become tahor.
chunks.st: And if the nazirite is in the days of his counting,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the seven days a leper must count after purification from his leprosy;

chunks.en: and the days of his full tzaraas:
chunks.st: or in his days of full leprosy, when he is a full-fledged leper,

chunks.en: for these, the nazir does not shave.
chunks.st: for these the nazirite does not shave.
chunks.stMore: This is the case even if he is rendered impure by one of the sources listed in the previous mishna.

chunks.en: He is sprinkled on the third and seventh days,
chunks.st: And in those cases listed that involve ritual impurity from a corpse, one sprinkles the purification water upon him on the third and on the seventh days of his purification,

chunks.en: he does not undo the days before,
chunks.st: and he does not negate the earlier
chunks.stMore: days of his naziriteship, but they are considered part of his naziriteship term.

chunks.en: he starts counting right away,
chunks.st: And he starts counting the rest of his naziriteship to complete his term immediately after his purification,

chunks.en: and he has no korban.
chunks.st: and he has no obligation to sacrifice an offering
chunks.stMore: of impurity for these sources of ritual impurity.

chunks.en: Truly they said:
chunks.st: Actually they said an ancient tradition that these

chunks.en: the days of a zav and a zavah
chunks.st: days of the impurity of the zav (Leviticus 15:1–15) and the zava (Leviticus 15:25–30)

words.note: A person with a kind of tumah that comes from the body.

chunks.en: and the days a metzora is shut away to be checked
chunks.st: and the days of the confinement of a leper
chunks.stMore: before he is confirmed as a full-fledged leper (Leviticus 13:4–5)

chunks.en: count for him.
chunks.explain: They count as days of his nezirus.
chunks.st: count for him toward the period of his naziriteship.

mishnayos.stIntro: The previous mishna listed the sources of ritual impurity for which a nazirite must shave. This mishna adds:

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Eliezer teaches that the tumah that makes a nazir shave is the tumah that forbids going into the Mikdash. Rabbi Akiva tells how he tried to prove a rule with a kal vachomer, and Rabbi Yehoshua said it is a halachah from long ago.

chunks.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: any tumah from a dead person
chunks.st: With regard to any ritual impurity from a corpse

chunks.en: that a nazir shaves for,
chunks.st: for which a nazirite must shave,

chunks.en: one is punished for going into the Mikdash with it.
chunks.st: one is liable due to the prohibition of entering the Temple
chunks.stMore: after contracting that impurity. If someone who became impure from one of those sources of impurity enters the Temple, he violates the prohibition against an impure individual entering the sacred space.

chunks.en: And any tumah from a dead person
chunks.st: And with regard to any impurity from a corpse

chunks.en: that a nazir does not shave for,
chunks.st: for which a nazirite does not shave,

chunks.he: אֵין חַיָּבִין עָלֶיהָ עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ.
chunks.en: one is not punished for going into the Mikdash with it.
chunks.st: one is likewise not liable due to the prohibition of entering the Temple after contracting it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:

chunks.he: לֹא תְהֵא זוֹ קַלָּה מִן הַשֶּׁרֶץ.
chunks.en: "This should not be lighter than a sheretz!"
chunks.explain: One who touched a sheretz may not go into the Mikdash.
chunks.st: This impurity from a corpse that does not obligate a nazirite to shave should not be more lenient than the impurity of a creeping animal.
chunks.stMore: The Torah clearly states that one rendered impure from a creeping animal is prohibited from entering the Temple (see Leviticus 5:2–3). The mishna continues to address the sources of ritual impurity for which a nazirite must shave.

words.note: A small creeping animal, like a mouse, that makes things tamei.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva said:

chunks.en: "I argued before Rabbi Eliezer:
chunks.st: I discussed this matter before Rabbi Eliezer
chunks.stMore: and suggested the following a fortiori inference:

chunks.en: If a bone the size of a barley grain,
chunks.st: If, with regard to a bone that is a barley-grain-bulk,

chunks.en: which does not make a person tamei under one roof,
chunks.st: which does not render a person impure in a tent,

chunks.he: הַנָּזִיר מְגַלֵּחַ עַל מַגָּעוֹ וְעַל מַשָּׂאוֹ.
chunks.en: makes a nazir shave for touching it or carrying it,
chunks.st: a nazirite must nevertheless shave for touching it or carrying it,

chunks.he: רְבִיעִית דָּם שֶׁהוּא מְטַמֵּא אָדָם בְּאֹהֶל,
chunks.en: then a revi'is of blood, which does make a person tamei under one roof,
chunks.st: then in the case of a quarter-log of blood, which is more stringent in that it renders a person impure in a tent,

chunks.en: surely the nazir should shave
chunks.st: is it not logical that a nazirite should shave

chunks.en: for touching it or carrying it!
chunks.st: for touching it or carrying it?

chunks.en: He said to me,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer said to me:

chunks.en: 'What is this, Akiva?
chunks.st: What is this, Akiva?

chunks.en: We do not use a kal vachomer here.'
chunks.st: One cannot argue by means of an a fortiori inference here,
chunks.stMore: in this particular case. However, Rabbi Eliezer did not provide a reason for this response.

words.note: Kal vachomer: if a lighter thing has a rule, a stricter thing surely has it.

chunks.en: When I came and told these things
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva continued: And when I came and presented these matters

chunks.en: before Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: before Rabbi Yehoshua,

chunks.en: he said to me,
chunks.st: he said to me:

chunks.en: 'You said it well,
chunks.st: You spoke well, i.e., your logic is flawless,

chunks.en: but this is how they taught it as a halachah.'"
chunks.explain: It is a halachah from Moshe at Sinai, so we do not argue against it.
chunks.st: but they indeed said that this is a halakha
chunks.stMore: transmitted to Moses from Sinai, which cannot be refuted by means of an a fortiori inference.

mishnayos.summary: Two nazirs were told that one of them became tamei, but nobody knows which one. The mishnah teaches how they bring korbanos together so each one brings what he needs, what to do if one of them dies, and Ben Zoma's simpler way.

chunks.en: Two nazirs, and someone said to them,
chunks.st: With regard to two nazirites, where one other person said to them:

chunks.en: "I saw one of you become tamei,
chunks.st: I saw one of you become impure,

chunks.en: but I don't know which of you":
chunks.st: but I do not know which one of you it was,

chunks.he: מְגַלְּחִין וּמְבִיאִין קָרְבַּן טֻמְאָה וְקָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה,
chunks.en: they shave and bring a korban of tumah and a korban of taharah.
chunks.explain: They bring them together, because no one knows who is tamei.
chunks.st: they must each complete their naziriteship terms, shave their hair, and both together bring an offering of ritual impurity and an offering of purity, due to the uncertainty.

chunks.en: And one says, "If I am the tamei one,
chunks.st: And one of them says to the other: If I am the impure one,

chunks.he: קָרְבַּן טֻמְאָה שֶׁלִּי וְקָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה שֶׁלְּךָ.
chunks.en: the korban of tumah is mine and the korban of taharah is yours.
chunks.st: the offering of impurity is mine and the offering of purity is yours;

chunks.en: And if I am the tahor one,
chunks.st: and if I am the pure one,

chunks.he: קָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה שֶׁלִּי וְקָרְבַּן טֻמְאָה שֶׁלְּךָ.
chunks.en: the korban of taharah is mine and the korban of tumah is yours."
chunks.st: the offering of purity is mine and the offering of impurity is yours.

chunks.en: Then they count thirty days
chunks.st: And because of the uncertainty they each count a further thirty days of naziriteship

chunks.en: and bring a korban of taharah,
chunks.st: and both together bring an offering of purity.

chunks.en: and one says, "If I am the tamei one,
chunks.st: And one of them says: If I am the previously impure one,

chunks.en: the korban of tumah was mine,
chunks.st: that offering of impurity sacrificed earlier was mine,

chunks.en: and the korban of taharah was yours,
chunks.st: and the offering of purity was yours;

chunks.en: and this is my korban of taharah.
chunks.st: and this offering sacrificed now is my offering of purity.

chunks.en: And if I am the tahor one,
chunks.st: And if I am the previously pure one,

chunks.en: the korban of taharah was mine,
chunks.st: the offering of purity brought earlier was mine,

chunks.en: and the korban of tumah was yours,
chunks.st: and the offering of impurity was yours;

chunks.en: and this is your korban of taharah."
chunks.st: and this current offering is your offering of purity.
chunks.stMore: The previous mishna described how two nazirites sacrifice offerings of impurity and purity, in a situation in which one of them has become impure but they do not know which one.

chunks.en: If one of them died,
chunks.st: This mishna discusses what must be done if one of them dies before bringing his offerings.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said:

chunks.en: he should ask someone from the marketplace
chunks.st: The surviving nazirite asks someone in the marketplace, a non-nazirite,

chunks.en: to promise to be a nazir together with him,
chunks.st: to vow to be a nazirite corresponding to him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., under the same conditions as his own naziriteship, so that he can bring offerings together with him.

chunks.en: and he says, "If I was tamei,
chunks.st: And he says to him as follows: If I was impure,

chunks.en: you are a nazir right away.
chunks.st: you are hereby a nazirite immediately;

chunks.en: And if I was tahor,
chunks.st: and if I was pure,

chunks.he: הֲרֵי אַתָּה נָזִיר אַחַר שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם.
chunks.en: you are a nazir after thirty days."
chunks.st: you are hereby a nazirite after thirty days.

chunks.en: They count thirty days
chunks.st: And they both proceed to count thirty days

chunks.en: and bring a korban of tumah and a korban of taharah,
chunks.st: and bring an offering of impurity and an offering of purity.

chunks.en: and he says, "If I am the tamei one,
chunks.st: And the nazirite who was defined as having uncertain impurity says: If I am the impure one,

chunks.he: קָרְבַּן טֻמְאָה שֶׁלִּי וְקָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה שֶׁלְּךְ.
chunks.en: the korban of tumah is mine and the korban of taharah is yours.
chunks.st: the offering of impurity is mine and the offering of purity is yours;

chunks.en: And if I am the tahor one,
chunks.st: and if I am the pure one,

chunks.he: קָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה שֶׁלִּי וְקָרְבַּן טֻמְאָה בְּסָפֵק.
chunks.en: the korban of taharah is mine, and the korban of tumah is a "maybe."
chunks.explain: Maybe he was tahor, and the friend who died was the tamei one.
chunks.st: the offering of purity is mine and the offering of impurity we brought shall be of uncertain status.

chunks.he: וְסוֹפְרִין שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם וּמְבִיאִין קָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה,
chunks.en: Then they count thirty days and bring a korban of taharah,
chunks.st: And they subsequently count another thirty days and bring an offering of purity,

chunks.en: and he says, "If I am the tamei one,
chunks.st: and the first nazirite says: If I was the impure one,

chunks.en: the korban of tumah was mine,
chunks.st: the offering of impurity that we sacrificed at the end of the first thirty days was mine,

chunks.en: and the korban of taharah was yours,
chunks.st: and the offering of purity we brought then was yours;

chunks.en: and this is my korban of taharah.
chunks.st: and this offering I am bringing now is my offering of purity.

chunks.en: And if I am the tahor one,
chunks.st: And if I was the pure one, and the deceased nazirite was impure,

chunks.en: the korban of taharah was mine,
chunks.st: the offering of purity we brought thirty days ago was mine,

chunks.en: and the korban of tumah was a "maybe,"
chunks.st: and the offering of impurity we brought earlier was of uncertain status,

chunks.en: and this is your korban of taharah."
chunks.st: and this is your offering of purity.

chunks.en: Ben Zoma said to him,
chunks.st: Ben Zoma said to Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.he: וּמִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לוֹ שֶׁיִּדֹּר כְּנֶגְדּוֹ בְנָזִיר.
chunks.en: "And who will listen to him and promise to be a nazir together with him?
chunks.st: And who will listen to him to vow to be a nazirite corresponding to him?
chunks.stMore: How can one design a halakha on the assumption that a non-nazirite will agree to be a nazirite for a lengthy term?

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מֵבִיא חַטַּאת הָעוֹף וְעוֹלַת בְּהֵמָה,
chunks.en: Rather, he brings a bird chatas and an animal olah,
chunks.st: Rather, a different procedure is available: After thirty days of naziriteship he brings a bird sin-offering and an animal burnt-offering,

chunks.en: and says, 'If I was tamei,
chunks.st: and says: If I was impure,

chunks.en: the chatas is what I owe, and the olah is a gift.
chunks.st: the sin-offering is for my obligation as an impure nazirite, and the burnt-offering is a regular gift offering.

chunks.en: And if I was tahor,
chunks.st: And if I was pure,

chunks.en: the olah is what I owe, and the chatas is a maybe.'
chunks.st: the burnt-offering is for my obligation as a pure nazirite, and the sin-offering is of uncertain status.

chunks.he: וְסוֹפֵר שְׁלשִׁים יוֹם וּמֵבִיא קָרְבַּן טָהֳרָה,
chunks.en: Then he counts thirty days and brings a korban of taharah,
chunks.st: And he counts another thirty days, and brings an offering of purity,

chunks.en: and says, 'If I was tamei,
chunks.st: and says: If I was impure,

chunks.en: the first olah was a gift, and this one is what I owe.
chunks.st: the first burnt-offering I brought should be considered a gift offering, and this one I am bringing now is for my obligation.

chunks.en: And if I was tahor,
chunks.st: And if I was pure,

chunks.en: the first olah was what I owe, and this one is a gift,
chunks.st: the first burnt-offering I brought is for my obligation as a pure nazirite, and this one I am bringing now is a gift offering.

chunks.en: and these are the rest of my korbanos.'"
chunks.st: And these, i.e., the sin-offering and peace-offering I am sacrificing now, comprises the rest of my offerings that I was obligated to bring earlier.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua said: According to your opinion,

chunks.en: "It turns out that he brings his korbanos in halves."
chunks.st: it turns out that this nazirite brings his offerings in halves,
chunks.stMore: i.e., in stages. If he was pure, he brings his burnt-offering thirty days before the rest of his offerings.

chunks.he: אֲבָל הוֹדוּ לוֹ חֲכָמִים לְבֶן זוֹמָא:
chunks.en: But the Sages agreed with Ben Zoma.
chunks.st: However, the Rabbis agreed with ben Zoma,
chunks.stMore: and disregarded the concern about splitting up the offerings.

mishnayos.summary: A nazir who might be tamei and might also be a metzora must wait a long time before he may eat holy food and before his nezirus ends, because we are not sure about either one.

chunks.he: נָזִיר שֶׁהָיָה טָמֵא בְסָפֵק וּמֻחְלָט בְּסָפֵק,
chunks.en: A nazir who might be tamei, and might be a full metzora,
chunks.st: In the case of a nazirite who, on the first day of his naziriteship, was impure from a corpse as a matter of uncertainty and was also a confirmed leper as a matter of uncertainty,
chunks.stMore: i.e., it was uncertain whether or not he had leprosy, how can he fulfill the shaving obligations of a pure nazirite and an impure leper? The problem facing this nazirite is that a leper must shave both when he begins his purification process and at the close of it, one week later. However, a nazirite is prohibited from shaving. Additionally, a leper may not partake of sacrificial food, but a nazirite may.

chunks.en: may eat kodashim after sixty days,
chunks.explain: He shaves for his tzaraas after thirty days, and again after thirty more.
chunks.st: Therefore, he may partake of sacrificial food sixty days after
chunks.stMore: he may have become impure, when the uncertainty with regard to leprosy will have been clarified. He shaves for the first time for his leprosy after thirty days, and for the second time thirty days later, the shaving of the end of the purification process; at which point he brings the offerings of a purified leper and may partake of sacrificial food.

words.note: Holy food from korbanos.

chunks.en: and may drink wine and become tamei from dead people
chunks.st: But he may drink wine and become impure from the dead, effectively ending his naziriteship, only

chunks.en: only after a hundred and twenty days,
chunks.st: after 120 days.
chunks.stMore: This is because he might have been a full-fledged leper, which means that his shavings count toward his leprosy, not his naziriteship. Consequently, after the first sixty days he must observe another thirty days of naziriteship and shave again. Even then he has yet to fulfill all his obligations, as he might have been impure from a corpse, which means his shaving after ninety days was for his impurity. He must therefore remain a nazirite for another thirty days, before shaving one final time at the end of 120 days to fulfill his naziriteship obligation. The mishna notes: The reason that he cannot shave for his leprosy after seven days and perform the second shaving of a leper seven days later is

chunks.en: because the shaving for tzaraas pushes aside
chunks.st: because the shaving of leprosy overrides

chunks.en: the nazir's shaving
chunks.st: the prohibition of the shaving of a nazirite

chunks.en: only when he surely has tzaraas.
chunks.st: only when his status as a leper is definite.

chunks.he: אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא סָפֵק אֵינָהּ דּוֹחָה:
chunks.en: But when it is not sure, it does not push it aside.
chunks.st: However, when his status as a leper is uncertain, the shaving does not override his naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: and therefore he must wait thirty days before each of his shavings for leprosy.

mishnayos.summary: Non-Jews cannot become nazirs, but women and servants can. The mishnah compares how a husband and a master can stop their nezirus.

chunks.en: Non-Jews do not have nezirus.
chunks.st: Gentiles do not have naziriteship,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the halakhot of naziriteship do not apply to gentiles. They are not subject to the prohibitions of a nazirite, nor does one accept their offerings at the end of naziriteship.

chunks.en: Women and servants do have nezirus.
chunks.st: However, women and Canaanite slaves do have naziriteship.

words.note: Here: a non-Jewish servant who belongs to a Jewish master.

chunks.en: Women are stricter than servants,
chunks.st: The mishna adds: There is a greater stringency in the case of women than in the case of slaves,

chunks.en: because a master can force his servant,
chunks.explain: He can make him drink wine, even though he promised nezirus.
chunks.st: as a master may force his slave
chunks.stMore: to drink wine, shave his hair, or become ritually impure from a corpse, despite the slave’s vow of naziriteship,

chunks.en: but a husband cannot force his wife.
chunks.st: but a husband cannot force his wife
chunks.stMore: to transgress her naziriteship. The previous mishna taught that the naziriteship of women includes a stringency that does not apply to slaves.

chunks.en: Servants are stricter than women,
chunks.st: This mishna adds: There is a greater stringency in the case of slaves than in the case of women,

chunks.en: because a man can cancel his wife's promises,
chunks.st: as a man can nullify the vows of his wife

chunks.en: but he cannot cancel his servant's promises.
chunks.st: but he cannot nullify the vows of his slave,
chunks.stMore: despite the fact that he can prevent him from fulfilling them in practice.

chunks.en: If he canceled his wife's,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he nullified the naziriteship of his wife

chunks.en: it is canceled forever.
chunks.st: it is permanently nullified,
chunks.stMore: and it remains nullified even if she is later divorced or widowed.

chunks.en: If he canceled his servant's,
chunks.st: Conversely, if he nullified the naziriteship of his slave
chunks.stMore: by forcing him to violate the terms of his vow of naziriteship,

chunks.en: when he goes free, he finishes his nezirus.
chunks.st: when the slave is emancipated he completes his naziriteship.
chunks.stMore: In a case where a slave took a vow of naziriteship but was prevented by his master from fulfilling the terms of his vow, the Sages engaged in a dispute what the halakha would be if he permanently

chunks.en: If he ran away from his master,
chunks.st: left his master’s presence, i.e., he ran away without being emancipated.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he may not drink wine.
chunks.st: He may not drink wine.
chunks.stMore: Since the slave is free in practice, his vow goes into effect.

chunks.en: And Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: And Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: he may drink.
chunks.st: He may drink wine, as he is not emancipated.

mishnayos.summary: If a nazir finds out after shaving that he had been tamei, it depends on whether the tumah was known or hidden. The mishnah gives the example of a dead body found in a cave where someone went into the water.

chunks.he: נָזִיר שֶׁגִּלַּח וְנוֹדַע לוֹ שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא,
chunks.en: A nazir who shaved, and then found out he had been tamei:
chunks.st: With regard to a nazirite who shaved for the conclusion of his naziriteship, and it later became known to him that during his naziriteship he was ritually impure from a corpse,

chunks.en: if it was a known tumah, it undoes his days.
chunks.st: if it was a known impurity, i.e., people were aware of the impurity when he became impure, he negates his entire naziriteship.

chunks.en: But if it was a tumah from the deep,
chunks.explain: A tumah nobody knew about, like a hidden grave.
chunks.st: And if it was ritual impurity imparted by a grave in the depths, one that was unknown at the time,

chunks.en: it does not undo them.
chunks.st: he does not negate his naziriteship.

chunks.en: If he found out before he shaved,
chunks.st: If he discovered he was impure before he shaved,

chunks.en: either way it undoes his days.
chunks.st: he negates his naziriteship in either case.

chunks.en: How is it? If he went down to tovel in a cave,
chunks.st: The mishna asks: How does one differentiate between a known and an unknown impurity? If a nazirite descended to immerse in a cave,

chunks.he: וְנִמְצָא מֵת צָף עַל פִּי הַמְּעָרָה,
chunks.en: and a dead body was found floating at the top of the cave,
chunks.st: and a corpse was found floating at the mouth of the cave,

chunks.en: he is tamei.
chunks.explain: Everyone could see it, so it is a known tumah.
chunks.st: he is impure,
chunks.stMore: as an openly visible corpse is a known impurity. What, then, is an impurity of the depths? This is referring to a case where the corpse

chunks.en: If it was found sunk into the floor of the cave:
chunks.st: was found sunk into the ground of the cave
chunks.stMore: in such a manner that it was unknown. However, even here the circumstances of the case must be taken into account.

chunks.en: if he went down to cool off, he is tahor.
chunks.st: If one descended not to immerse himself in the water, as he was ritually pure, but to cool himself, he remains pure.

chunks.en: If he went in to become tahor from the tumah of a dead body, he is tamei,
chunks.st: If he was impure and entered the water to purify himself from the impurity from a corpse, he is impure.

chunks.en: because one who was tamei stays tamei,
chunks.st: The reason is that something that has the presumptive status of impurity remains impure,

chunks.en: and one who was tahor stays tahor,
chunks.st: and something that has the presumptive status of purity is pure,

chunks.en: since there is a reason to say so.
chunks.st: as there is a basis for the matter.
chunks.stMore: It is reasonable that items or people retain their presumptive status.

mishnayos.summary: If someone finds a buried body in a field, he may move it together with the earth around it. If he finds three, it may be an old cemetery, and he must check the area around them.

chunks.en: Someone who finds a dead body for the first time, lying the usual way,
chunks.explain: Lying the way Jews are buried.
chunks.st: One who finds a corpse for the first time, i.e., he discovers a single corpse in a place that was not previously established as a cemetery, if the corpse is lying in the usual manner of Jewish burial,

chunks.en: may take it away with the earth around it.
chunks.st: he removes it from there and also its surrounding earth.
chunks.stMore: It is assumed that this corpse was buried there alone. There is no concern that this area is a cemetery and therefore the corpse may not be moved, nor does one take into account the possibility that another corpse may be buried in the vicinity.

chunks.en: If he found two,
chunks.st: Similarly, if he found two corpses,

chunks.en: he takes them away with the earth around them.
chunks.st: he removes them and their surrounding earth.

chunks.en: If he found three,
chunks.st: In a case where he found three corpses,

chunks.en: if between one and the next
chunks.st: if there is a space between this corpse and that corpse

chunks.en: there are four to eight amos,
chunks.st: of four to eight cubits, in a standard design,

chunks.en: this is a cemetery.
chunks.st: this is a graveyard.
chunks.stMore: There is a concern that this might be an ancient cemetery.

chunks.en: He must check twenty amos farther out from there.
chunks.st: One must therefore examine from that spot outward for twenty cubits.

chunks.en: If he found another one at the end of twenty amos,
chunks.st: If one finds another corpse at the end of twenty cubits,

chunks.en: he checks twenty amos farther out from there,
chunks.st: he examines from that spot outward twenty cubits,

chunks.en: because there is a reason to think so,
chunks.st: as there is a basis for anticipating the matter.
chunks.stMore: It is likely that he has stumbled upon an ancient gravesite. He is not permitted to relocate the corpses, despite the fact

chunks.en: even though if he had found it alone at first,
chunks.st: that if he had found the single corpse by itself at first

chunks.en: he could have taken it away with the earth around it.
chunks.st: he could have removed it and its surrounding earth.

mishnayos.summary: When we are not sure about tzaraas, it is tahor at first, but once a person is tamei, a doubt is tamei. The same idea is taught about a zav, and about a man who hurt another man who later died.

chunks.en: Any doubt about tzaraas marks, at first,
is tahor until it is decided to be tamei.
Once it was decided to be tamei,
a doubt about it is tamei.
In seven ways we check a zav

words.note: A person with a kind of tumah that comes from the body.

chunks.en: before he is decided to be a zav:
chunks.explain: We check if something else caused it.

chunks.en: food and drink,
carrying something heavy and jumping,
sickness, and what he saw or thought about.
Once he was decided to be a zav,
we do not check him anymore.
Then all the tumah that comes from him is tamei,
since there is a reason to say so.
If someone hit another man, and they thought he would die,
and he got better than he was,
and later he got worse and died, the one who hit him is chayav.
chunks.explain: We say the hitting caused his death.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says he is patur,
since there is a reason to say so.
chunks.explain: He got better, so maybe something else caused his death.

mishnayos.summary: Rabbi Nehorai says that Shmuel HaNavi was a nazir, because the pasuk says "a morah will not go up on his head," just like it says about Shimshon. Rabbi Yosei asks if "morah" means fear.

chunks.en: Shmuel was a nazir,
chunks.st: Samuel the prophet was a nazirite,

words.note: Shmuel HaNavi.

chunks.en: as Rabbi Nehorai says,
chunks.st: in accordance with the statement of Rabbi Nehorai,

chunks.en: as it says, "And a morah
chunks.explain: Chanah promised this when she davened for a son.
chunks.st: as it was stated
chunks.stMore: that when Hannah, his mother, prayed for a son, she vowed:

chunks.en: will not go up on his head."
chunks.st: “And no mora shall come upon his head”
chunks.stMore: (I Samuel 1:11). How is it derived that mora is an expression of naziriteship?

chunks.en: It says about Shimshon, "And a morah,"
chunks.explain: There, morah means a razor.
chunks.st: It is stated with regard to Samson: “And no razor [mora]
chunks.stMore: shall come upon his head, for the child shall be a nazirite to God” (Judges 13:5),

chunks.en: and it says about Shmuel, "And a morah."
chunks.st: and it is stated: “And no mora,” with regard to Samuel.

chunks.en: Just as the "morah" said about Shimshon means a nazir,
chunks.st: Just as the term “mora” that is stated with regard to Samson means that he was a nazirite,

chunks.en: so too the "morah" said about Shmuel means a nazir.
chunks.st: so too the term “mora” that is stated with regard to Samuel indicates that he was a nazirite.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.he: וַהֲלֹא אֵין מוֹרָה אֶלָּא שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם.
chunks.en: "But doesn't 'morah' just mean fear of people?"
chunks.explain: He reads morah as "fear," not "razor."
chunks.st: But doesn’t the word “mora” mean nothing other than the fear of flesh and blood?
chunks.stMore: The word should be read as though it were written with an alef, and not a heh, so that it means fear.

chunks.en: Rabbi Nehorai said to him,
chunks.st: Rabbi Nehorai said to him:

chunks.en: "But it already says,
chunks.st: But isn’t it already stated: “

chunks.en: 'And Shmuel said: How can I go?
chunks.st: And Samuel said: How can I go;

chunks.en: Shaul will hear and kill me.'
chunks.st: if Saul hears it he will kill me” (I Samuel 16:2).

chunks.he: שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה עָלָיו מוֹרָה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם:
chunks.en: So he was already afraid of people!"
chunks.explain: So morah must mean a razor, and Shmuel was a nazir.
chunks.st: This verse indicates that there was fear of flesh and blood upon Samuel.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, the term mora must be understood in accordance with its plain meaning of a razor. If so, Samuel was indeed a nazirite.

mishnayos.stIntro: The tractate concludes with an aggadic statement about nazirites.
